input.quote: MSL agrees that MSL engineering will be priced to IBM on a "most favored customer" basis.
input.rationale: The only most-favoured-nation mechanic in the Agreement runs in our favour: MSL must price its engineering to IBM on a "most favored customer" basis (p1099). Targeted searches for reciprocal language ("no less favorable", "more favorable terms", "best price", "favorable", "match", "preferential", "lowest") return nothing that obliges IBM to extend MSL terms given to third parties. The adjacent right-to-match on tooling (p1104) and the right of first refusal (p1230) likewise benefit IBM, and MSL's low-cost purchasing undertaking (p0821) is a Vendor obligation. This meets the preferred position — Customer has no MFN obligation benefiting Vendor — so no redline is proposed and the Vendor-granted MFN is retained.
